facts.text: In the period after 1857, Ramsinh Kuka organised a rebellion against the Government in Punjab.
facts.quote: In the later period, Ramsinh Kuka organised a rebellion against the Government in Punjab.

facts.text: In Maharashtra, Vasudev Balwant Phadke gave an armed struggle against the British; he took the training of arms from Vastad Lahuji Salve.
facts.quote: In Maharashtra, Vasudev Balwant Phadke gave an armed struggle against the British. ... He took the training of arms from Vastad Lahuji Salve.

facts.text: Vasudev Balwant Phadke organised the Ramoshis and revolted against the British; the rebellion was unsuccessful.
facts.quote: He organised the Ramoshis and revolted against the British. This rebellion became unsuccessful.

facts.text: The British Government sent Vasudev Balwant Phadke to Eden jail, where he died in 1883.
facts.quote: The British Government sent him to Eden jail. There he died in 1883.

facts.text: In 1897 Plague Commissioner Rand resorted to tyranny and force while managing the plague epidemic in Pune.
facts.quote: In 1897, the Plague Commissioner Rand had resorted to tyranny and force while managing the epidemic of plague in Pune.

facts.text: As a revenge, the Chafekar brothers Damodar and Balkrishna shot Rand dead on 22 June 1897.
facts.quote: As a revenge the Chafekar brothers, Damodar and Balkrishna, shot him dead on 22 June 1897.

facts.text: Damodar, Balkrishna and Vasudev Chafekar and their associate Mahadev Ranade were hanged; three brothers from the same house accepted martyrdom.
facts.quote: Damodar, Balkrishna and Vasudev these three brothers and their associate Mahadev Ranade were hanged to death. From the same house, three brothers accepted martyrdom for the service of the country.

facts.text: During the same period, the Munda tribe in Bihar under Birsa Munda made a great revolt against the Government.
facts.quote: During the same period Munda tribe in Bihar under the leadership of Birsa Munda made great revolt against the Government.

facts.text: In 1900 Swatantryaveer Vinayak Damodar Savarkar founded 'Mitramela', a secret organisation of revolutionaries in Nasik.
facts.quote: In 1900, Swatantryaveer Vinayak Damodar Savarkar founded 'Mitramela'- a secret organisation of revolutionaries in Nasik.

facts.text: Mitramela was renamed 'Abhinav Bharat' in 1904.
facts.quote: The same organisation was renamed as 'Abhinav Bharat' in 1904.

facts.text: Savarkar went to England for higher education and from there sent revolutionary literature and guns to members of Abhinav Bharat in India.
facts.quote: Savarkar went to England for higher education. From there he began sending revolutionary literature, guns etc. to the members of Abhinav Bharat in India.

facts.text: Savarkar wrote an inspiring biography of Joseph Mazzini, the famous Italian revolutionary.
facts.quote: He wrote an inspiring biography of Joseph Mazzini, the famous Italian revolutionary.

facts.text: Savarkar wrote 'The 1857 War of Independence', stating that the revolt of 1857 was the first war of independence.
facts.quote: He wrote a book entitled 'The 1857 War of Independence' wherein he stated that revolt of 1857 was the first war of independence.

facts.text: Savarkar was sentenced to fifty years of rigorous imprisonment at Andaman; he was there for ten years.
facts.quote: Swatantryaveer Savarkar was sentenced to fifty years of rigorous imprisonment at Andaman. He was there for ten years.

facts.text: In his autobiography 'Majhi Janmathep', Savarkar wrote about his terrible days in Andaman.
facts.quote: In his autobiography 'Majhi Janmathep' he wrote down his experiences of the terrible days in Andaman.

facts.text: The Government detained Savarkar at Ratnagiri, where he started social movements such as removal of caste differences, removal of untouchability, common dining and purification of language.
facts.quote: Later the Government took him to Ratnagiri and detained there. There Savarkar started many social movements such as removal of caste differences, removal of untouchability, common dining, purification of language etc.

facts.text: Savarkar was the President of the Marathi Sahitya Sammelan at Mumbai in 1938.
facts.quote: He was the President of Marathi Sahitya Sammelan at Mumbai in 1938.

facts.text: When the Government learnt about Abhinav Bharat, it arrested Babarao Savarkar, who was sentenced to life imprisonment.
facts.quote: The Government came to know about the activities of Abhinav Bharat. Therefore the Government arrested Babarao Savarkar. He was sentenced to life imprisonment.

facts.text: As a revenge, a youth named Anant Laxman Kanhere killed Jackson, the Collector of Nasik.
facts.quote: As a revenge to this punishment, a youth named Anant Laxman Kanhere killed Jackson, the Collector of Nasik.

facts.text: The Government linked Jackson's murder with Savarkar; he was tried and the court ordered rigorous punishment for 50 years.
facts.quote: The murder of Jackson was linked with Swatantryaveer Savarkar by the Government, he was arrested and put under trial. The court ordered him rigorous punishment for 50 years.

facts.text: After the partition of Bengal, the outrage against the British became more severe and revolutionary movements rose at the national level.
facts.quote: After the partition of Bengal, the outrage against British became more severe. In place of local rebellions comprehensive revolutionary movements started rising at national level.

facts.text: In Bengal the revolutionary organisation 'Anushilan Samiti' was active; it had more than 500 branches.
facts.quote: In Bengal a revolutionary organisation called 'Anushilan Samiti' was active. The Anushilan Samiti had more than 500 branches.

facts.text: Barindrakumar Ghosh, brother of Aurobindo Ghosh, was the chief of the Anushilan Samiti; it received counsel and guidance from Aurobindo Ghosh.
facts.quote: Barindrakumar Ghosh, brother of Aurobindo Ghosh, was the chief of this organisation. This organisation received counsel and guidance from Aurobindo Ghosh.

facts.text: The Anushilan Samiti had a bomb manufacturing centre at Maniktala near Kolkata.
facts.quote: The Anushilan Samiti had a bomb manufacturing centre at Maniktala near Kolkata.

facts.text: In 1908 Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki planned to kill a judge named Kingsford, but the bomb hit the wrong vehicle and two English women were killed.
facts.quote: In 1908, Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki, members of Anushilan Samiti planned to kill a judge named Kingsford. But the vehicle on which they threw the bomb was not the one carrying Kingsford. Two English women were killed in this attack.

facts.text: Prafulla Chaki shot himself so as not to fall into British hands; Khudiram Bose was caught by the police.
facts.quote: Prafulla Chaki shot himself with a bullet so that he will not fall in the hands of British. Khudiram Bose was caught by the police.

facts.text: Aurobindo Ghosh was arrested, but the Government could not link him to making bombs, so the court set him free.
facts.quote: Aurobindo Ghosh was also arrested. But the Government was unsuccessful in linking him to manufacturing of bombs and hence the court set him free.

facts.text: Rash Behari Bose and Sachindra Nath Sanyal spread revolutionary organisations outside Bengal, with centres in Punjab, Delhi and Uttar Pradesh.
facts.quote: Rash Behari Bose and Sachindra Nath Sanyal spread the network of revolutionary organisations outside Bengal. The centres of revolutionary work were set up at Punjab, Delhi and Uttar Pradesh.

facts.text: Rash Behari Bose and his associate threw a bomb at Viceroy Lord Hardinge, but he was saved.
facts.quote: Rash Behari Bose and his associate made a daring act of throwing bomb at the Viceroy Lord Hardinge. But he got saved from the attack.

facts.text: In Madras Province, revolutionary Vanchhi Iyyer killed a British officer named Ash and then shot himself.
facts.quote: The revolutionary work was carried out in Madras Province as well. Vanchhi Iyyer, a revolutionary, killed a British officer named Ash. Later he shot himself with a bullet and sacrificed his own life.

facts.text: India House in London was established by Pandit Shyamji Krishna Varma; through it Indian youths, including Savarkar, got scholarships for higher education in England.
facts.quote: India House, in London, was an important centre ... Pandit Shyamji Krishna Varma, an Indian patriot, had established India House. Through this organisation Indian youths were given scholarships for higher education in England. Swatantryaveer Savarkar received such scholarship.

facts.text: Madam Cama raised the issue of India's independence at the World Socialist Conference at Stuttgart in Germany and unfurled the flag of India there.
facts.quote: Madam Cama raised the issue of India's independence at the World Socialist Conference held at Stuttgart in Germany. In the same conference she unfurled the flag of India.

facts.text: Madanlal Dhingra, a youth associated with India House, killed British officer Curzon Wylie and was hanged.
facts.quote: Another revolutionary associated with India House was a youth named Madanlal Dhingra. He killed Curzon Wylie, a British Officer, due to which Dhingra was hanged to death.

facts.text: Indians living in America and Canada established the Gadar organisation; Lala Hardayal, Bhai Parmanand and Dr. Pandurang Sadashiv Khankhoje were important leaders.
facts.quote: The Indians living in America and Canada established the Gadar organisation. Lala Hardayal, Bhai Parmanand, Dr. Pandurang Sadashiv Khankhoje etc. these revolutionaries were the important leaders of the organisation.

facts.text: The word 'Gadar' means 'revolt'; 'Gadar' was also the journal (mouthpiece) of the organisation.
facts.quote: The word 'Gadar' means 'revolt'. 'Gadar' was the journal of this organisation that acted as its mouthpiece.

facts.text: Gadar leaders planned a revolt in Punjab to be led by Rash Behari Bose and Vishnu Ganesh Pingle; due to treachery Pingle was caught and hanged, while Rash Behari Bose escaped to Japan.
facts.quote: It was decided that Rash Behari Bose and Vishnu Ganesh Pingle should lead the revolt. But due to treachery, the British traced out the plan. Pingle fell into the hands of the police. He was hanged to death. But Rash Behari Bose escaped successfuly. He went to Japan

facts.text: In Berlin, Veerendra Nath Chattopadhyay, Bhupen Dutta and Hardayal prepared anti British plans with the German Foreign ministry.
facts.quote: In Berlin, Veerendra Nath Chattopadhyay, Bhupen Dutta and Hardayal prepared anti British plans in cooperation with the German Foreign ministry.

facts.text: In 1915 Mahendra Pratap, Barkatullah and Obaidullah Sindhi established the Provisional Government of free India in Kabul.
facts.quote: In 1915, Mahendra Pratap, Barkatullah and Obaidullah Sindhi established Provisional Government of free India in Kabul.

facts.text: After Mahatma Gandhi suspended the Civil Disobedience Movement, many youngsters turned to revolutionary ways.
facts.quote: After the suspension of Civil Disobedience Movement by Mahatma Gandhi, many youngsters got diverted to revolutionary ways.

facts.text: On 9 August 1925 Chandrashekhar Azad, Ram Prasad Bismil, Yogesh Chatterjee, Sachindra Nath Sanyal and others looted the Government treasury carried in a train near Kakori railway station in Uttar Pradesh: the 'Kakori conspiracy'.
facts.quote: On 9 August 1925, they looted the Government treasury that was carried in a train near Kakori railway station in Uttar Pradesh. This is known as the 'Kakori conspiracy'.

facts.text: Ashfaqulla Khan, Ram Prasad Bismil, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri were hanged, but Chandrashekhar Azad managed to escape.
facts.quote: Ashfaqulla Khan, Ram Prasad Bismil, Roshan Singh, Rajendra Lahiri were hanged. But Chandrashekhar Azad managed to escape.

facts.text: In 1928, at a meeting at Feroz Shah Kotla ground in Delhi, young men including Chandrashekhar Azad, Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev set up the 'Hindustan Socialist Republican Association'.
facts.quote: Prominent among them were Chandrashekhar Azad, Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, Sukhdev etc. ... In 1928 in the meeting held at Feroz Shah Kotla ground in Delhi, these young men established the organisation called 'Hindustan Socialist Republican Association'.

facts.text: The HSRA aimed to free India from British exploitation and overthrow the unjust system that exploited farmers and workers; Bhagat Singh stressed a society based on social justice and equality.
facts.quote: The objective behind the establishment of this organisation was to free India from British exploitation. It also wanted to overthrow the unjust socio-economic system which exploited the farmers and workers. Bhagat Singh gave importance to creation of a society based on social justice and equality.

facts.text: The wing for gathering arms was called the 'Hindustan Socialist Republican Army'; Chandrashekhar Azad was its chief.
facts.quote: This wing was called 'Hindustan Socialist Republican Army' and Chandrashekar Azad was the chief of this wing.

facts.text: Bhagat Singh and Rajguru killed an officer named Saunders to avenge the death of Lala Lajpat Rai.
facts.quote: Bhagat Singh and Rajguru fired bullets and killed an officer named Saunders in order to avenge the death of Lala Lajpat Rai.

facts.text: To protest two bills curtailing civil rights, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutta threw bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly.
facts.quote: The Government had introduced two bills in the Central Legislative Assembly, curtailing civil rights. To protest it, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutta threw bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly.

facts.text: On 23 March 1931 Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were hanged in the Lahore jail.
facts.quote: On 23 March 1931, Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were hanged in the Lahore jail.

facts.text: Chandrashekhar Azad never fell into police hands; he died in an encounter with police at Alfred Park in Allahabad.
facts.quote: But till the end Chandrashekhar Azad did not fall into the hands of the police. Later he died in an encounter with police at Alfred Park in Allahabad.

facts.text: Surya Sen was the chief of the revolutionary group at Chittagong in Bengal, with Anant Singh, Ganesh Ghosh, Kalpana Dutta and Pritilata Waddedar.
facts.quote: Surya Sen was the chief of the revolutionary group at Chittagong in Bengal. He had gathered around him revolutionaries like Anant Singh, Ganesh Ghosh, Kalpana Dutta, Pritilata Waddedar.

facts.text: On 18 April 1930 the revolutionaries seized arms from the two armouries in Chittagong and broke the telephone and telegraph lines.
facts.quote: As per the plan, on 18 April 1930 the revolutionaries seized the arms from the two armouries in Chittagong. The telephone and telegraph lines were broken

facts.text: On 16 February 1933 Surya Sen and some of his associates were captured by the police.
facts.quote: On 16 February 1933, Surya Sen and some of his associates were captured by the police.

facts.text: Surya Sen and his 12 associates were given death punishment; Kalpana Dutta got life imprisonment; Pritilata Waddedar killed herself rather than fall into police hands.
facts.quote: Surya Sen and his 12 associates were given death punishment. Kalpana Dutta was sentenced to life imprisonment. Pritilata Waddedar killed herself without falling into the hands of the police.

facts.text: School girls Shanti Ghosh and Suniti Choudhary killed the District Judge; young Bina Das shot the Governor during the convocation ceremony of Kolkata University.
facts.quote: Shanti Ghosh and Suniti Choudhary, these two school girls killed the District Judge, where as a young girl Bina Das shot dead the Governor during the convocation ceremony of Kolkata University.

facts.text: Sardar Udham Singh killed Dyer, the officer responsible for the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, in London in 1940.
facts.quote: Sardar Udham Singh killed Dyer, the officer responsible for Jallianwala Bagh massacre, in London in 1940.
